overview: Karnataka's coffee country: rolling estates, misty hills and quiet homestays around Mullayanagiri, Karnataka's highest peak. Slow-paced and green.
fit: Good for a relaxed break. Treks are short; the 4-year-old will enjoy estates, streams and animals at homestays.
season: October to March is cool (12–28°C). Heavy rain June–August makes roads slippery and leeches common.

gettingThere.detail: Chennai to Bengaluru by Shatabdi/Vande Bharat, then 5 hr drive; or overnight train to Kadur/Birur
Chennai to Mangaluru or Bengaluru, then drive

gettingAround: You need a car; homestays often arrange jeeps for estate roads.

todo.title: Coffee estate homestay
todo.why: Walk the estate, see how coffee is made
todo.book: Pick one with kid-friendly hosts and good reviews

todo.title: Mullayanagiri viewpoint
todo.why: Drive almost to the top, short climb
todo.book: Go early before mist and traffic

todo.title: Baba Budangiri
todo.why: Hills and caves on the same ridge

todo.title: Coffee Museum
todo.why: Short visit to learn about coffee

todo.title: Belur and Halebidu temples
todo.why: Exquisitely carved Hoysala temples on the way

todo.title: Jhari or Hebbe Falls by jeep
todo.why: Bumpy jeep ride to a waterfall
todo.book: Skip with the 4-year-old if roads are rough

foodTips: Homestays usually serve vegetarian on request and make mild food for kids.
save: Homestays with meals included are great value
Drive yourselves from Chennai if you're comfortable
Combine with Belur–Halebidu on the way
safety: Mist reduces visibility; avoid driving hill roads after dark
Keep kids away from estate ponds and open wells
kids: Many homestays have dogs, cows and chickens: a hit with the 4-year-old
Plan unhurried days with one outing each

days.plan: Travel to Chikmagalur; stop at Belur temple; check in
Mullayanagiri sunrise, estate walk, Coffee Museum
Jeep to a waterfall or lazy day at the homestay; Hirekolale sunset
Halebidu on the way back home
